transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Diego Ramos (Redwood SE); Priya Patel (Orchard Cloud - Head of ML Infra); Evan Li (Orchard Cloud - Cloud Architect); Sara Nguyen (Orchard Cloud - Security Lead)
---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, really appreciate it. quick intro, I'm Maya, AE on the account, and Diego is our systems engineer who will go deeper on networking and infra.
[00:12] Priya: Thanks, Maya. We are excited. I'm Priya, I own ML infra at Orchard Cloud, Evan is our cloud architect, Sara on security. We're looking at Private deployments for some regulated customers.
[00:23] Diego: Awesome. Real quick agenda \u2014 confirm requirements, go over networking options (VPC peering, PrivateLink / interface endpoints, private endpoints), region constraints, KMS and audit/logging, and next steps. Sound good?
[00:35] Evan: Yep. For context, we run primarily in us-east-1 and us-west-2, some customers need eu-west-1. Latency between region pairs is a concern; also we have strict egress rules and want no public internet egress for inference calls.
[00:50] Sara: And from security, SOC 2 plus customers asking for keys in our KMS and audit event forwarding to our SIEM, SAML SSO, RBAC \u2014 typical enterprise checklist.
[01:05] Maya: Great, that's aligned with what we've seen. Short answer: Redwood Private supports VPC peering and PrivateLink style private endpoints depending on your network model. We can run the control plane in Redwood-managed region with a private control channel or an on-prem control plane in more sensitive setups.
[01:20] Priya: When you say private endpoints, is that AWS PrivateLink? We prefer PrivateLink because it avoids broad route table changes.
[01:28] Diego: Yes, we support interface endpoints (PrivateLink) and also VPC peering for low-latency high-throughput setups. There's a tradeoff: peering gives quicker packet paths but requires more route table and CIDR planning; PrivateLink keeps control at the endpoint level and is easier for segmented networks.
[01:44] Evan: Do you do cross-account peering? We have separate accounts per environment and want to keep infra isolated.
[01:50] Diego: Yep, cross-account peering is fine. For peering we ask for your VPC CIDRs and we provision a peering connection from Redwood's VPC to the account VPC. For PrivateLink we create the service and you create an interface endpoint in your VPC. We can support both model types.
[02:05] Sara: How about DNS? Our apps resolve internal hostnames and we use split-horizon. We need the endpoints to be resolvable to private IPs.
[02:13] Diego: For PrivateLink, the interface endpoint creates elastic network interfaces in your subnets and local DNS hostnames. For peering, you will need to configure private hosted zones or conditional forwarding if you want canonical hostnames. We can provide suggested DNS records in the network checklist.
[02:30] Priya: And egress \u2014 we cannot allow traffic to go out to the public internet. Does Redwood require outbound internet for model pulls or telemetry?
[02:41] Maya: Good question. For Redwood Private, you can choose an architecture with no public egress: model artifacts can be pre-staged into your environment or we can push them over the private connection. Telemetry and metrics can be forwarded via private links; if you want absolutely zero egress you can opt for an air-gapped on-prem deployment but that's heavier.
[02:58] Evan: If we pre-stage model artifacts, do you support S3 presigned URLs cross-account or will Redwood push into a customer S3?
[03:07] Diego: We support a few modes: 1) you upload artifacts to a customer-owned S3 bucket and provide role access; 2) we pull via presigned URLs over the private connection; or 3) for Dedicated appliances we can ship artifacts as part of install. We'll outline recommended approach in the checklist.
[03:22] Priya: Region availability: You mentioned us-east-1/us-west-2/eu-west-1 \u2014 if our primary workloads are in eu-west-1, can Redwood's private control plane run in eu-west-1?
[03:32] Maya: We do have private deployment options in several regions; we'll confirm availability for eu-west-1. For strict data residency we can also offer a Private control plane hosted in your VPC (customer-managed control plane) \u2014 Diego can speak to constraints.
[03:45] Diego: The customer-managed control plane needs some minimal outbound for auth/cert rotation if you want fully managed but isolated; we can support an entirely private control plane in your VPC with KMS integration. That tends to be a longer onboarding (network, install, and ops).
[03:58] Sara: On KMS, customers want to control the root keys. Can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS customer-managed keys?
[04:06] Diego: Yes. We support CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) for data at rest. For some setups we integrate with your KMS via cross-account IAM roles; for HSM-backed keys we can connect to an external HSM if needed \u2014 we'll need network access and some config.
[04:19] Priya: Audit logs \u2014 we want all inference request metadata and admin actions forwarded into our Splunk. How does Redwood handle audit logging in Private?
[04:28] Maya: We can stream audit logs to a customer-owned endpoint \u2014 S3, Kinesis, or directly to your SIEM via secure forwarder. There are options to redact or pseudonymize sensitive fields before shipping if required. Diego: We'll provide the schema and expected event rate so you can size ingestion.
[04:45] Evan: What about throughput and latency? If we peer us-west-2 to your VPC in us-west-2, what latency targets do you typically hit?
[04:54] Diego: For same-region peering we typically see single-digit ms added for inference traffic; for cross-region it'll be whatever the inter-region peering imposes. For high-throughput needs we recommend Dedicated GPU pools colocated in your region to avoid cross-region hops.
[05:08] Priya: Pricing \u2014 is there an extra charge for PrivateLink or peering? Also for model hosting in a private deployment?
[05:16] Maya: There are architecture-specific costs: Private deployment has a platform fee and then infra (GPU, storage), plus any dedicated capacity commitment. PrivateLink itself has AWS interface endpoint charges on your side and some management fee. We'll include a pricing breakdown in the quote.
[05:29] Sara: Compliance docs \u2014 can you share SOC 2 and pen test reports?
[05:33] Maya: Absolutely. I'll share SOC 2 attestation, penetration test summary, and our security whitepaper. We'll also include the KMS integration guide and network checklist link.
[05:44] Evan: For the pilot, we'd like to run a small POC: 2-3 models, low QPS, traffic routed over PrivateLink in us-west-2, and metrics shipped to our Splunk. Timeline target: get POC started in January.
[05:57] Maya: That sounds reasonable. Typical pilot flow: network workshop and checklist -> provisioning (peering or PrivateLink) -> smaller dedicated pool or shared VM with pinned models -> run prompts and perf benchmarks -> iterate.
[06:10] Priya: Stakeholders: I'll be the exec sponsor, Evan owns the cloud/network config, Sara owns compliance, and Dev team will be involved later. We'll need an SOW and internal approval package.
[06:22] Maya: We'll prepare SOW draft and internal one-page for procurement. Any other blockers?
[06:27] Sara: A few compliance Qs I'll send ahead of workshop: data retention controls, PII handling, access logs retention periods.
[06:34] Diego: Noted. We'll prepare answers and examples. Also we'll ask for your VPC CIDR ranges, three subnets to place interface endpoints into, and any NACLs/security group constraints.
[06:47] Priya: One last networking nuance \u2014 we use Transit Gateway for account peering. Are you able to attach to TGW or do we need to create endpoints in each account?
[06:55] Diego: We can support TGW-based architectures; you'll need to allow the TGW to route to the subnets with interface endpoints. We'll call out TGW patterns in the checklist \u2014 some customers prefer TGW for scale.
[07:08] Maya: Ok wrapping up. Quick recap of next steps: I'll send the network checklist, SOC 2 and KMS docs, and a draft SOW/quote. Diego will schedule a technical workshop to walk the team through network setup. Evan will send CIDRs and region preferences. Sara will send compliance questions.
[07:24] Evan: Sounds good. Thanks Maya, Diego.
[07:27] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[07:30] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with links.
---
